newsitem.title: USA: High winds disrupt power to 40,000 N.Y. area users.
newsitem.headline: High winds disrupt power to 40,000 N.Y. area users.

text.p: About 40,000 electricity customers in the New York metropolitan area lost power early Thursday when strong winds whipped through the region, snapping tree limbs and bringing down overhead power lines.
The bulk of the outages were on Long Island, where gusts clocked at 65 miles per hour disrupted power service to 32,000 consumers.
Long Island Lighting Co (LILCO) said it was able to restore power to half of those customers by late morning.
LILCO supplies electricity to 1.1 million consumers.
"As the wind continues, we do not know when we could restore power to all customers," a LILCO spokeswoman said.

Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc (ConEd) said there were few outages in New York City, where there are also fewer trees, but 2,000 customers in suburban Westchester County, just north of the city, had lost service.
About 600 Westchester customers were still without electricity late this morning, a ConEd spokesman said.
Across the Hudson River in New Jersey, Public Service Electric and Gas Co (PSE&G) said high winds interrupted power in 10 municipalities in its central service territory.
"We had problems in the central part of the state," said a PSE&G spokesman, adding the lights were already back on at about 4,800 of the 5,500 customers whose service was affected.
PSE&G serves 2.2 million electric customers in a 2,600 square mile area across New Jersey.
"The (wind) system is not out of the area yet, so there could be more outages," the PSE&G spokesman warned.
